name: Single Pin Picking (SPP)
description: SPP involves applying light rotational tension to the cylinder with a tension wrench while using a hook pick to lift each pin stack individually to the shear line. Manufacturing tolerances cause pins to bind sequentially, allowing each pin to be set one at a time until the cylinder rotates. SPP is slower than raking but more reliable on quality locks and leaves fewer marks than raking or bumping. It is the primary technique for locks that require precise, quiet manipulation.

blue.det: Scratches around keyway; time spent at locked door without key use; picking sounds in quiet environments.
blue.cm: High-security cylinders (Medeco, Mul-T-Lock, Abloy) are pick-resistant; security pins increase difficulty; door alarms triggered by extended manipulation.
